lines.trans: Excuse me, sir: would you like to come inside for a warm cup of tea?
Wait... our neighbour from the violin shop at number ten?!
You two already know each other, Ernesto?!
Thirty years ago, he brought his violin here every Friday at six!

words.gloss: ago (hace treinta años = thirty years ago)

lines.trans: Wait, look at our old postcard: Save two chairs for the baker and the teacher!
He was the music teacher who played Friday duets with your aunt!
He just asked me who finally finished the second half of her May waltz!
What did he say when he heard my sixteen bars through the window, Ernesto?
He had tears in his eyes: he said it sounded just like her voice!
Did you invite him to our grand opening this Friday at six o'clock sharp?!
He promised to bring his violin and ten more neighbours from our street!
Ten more neighbours?! Rocio is going to need twice as many lemons by Friday!

You two already know each other, Ernesto?!
Thirty years ago, he brought his violin here every Friday at six!

lines.trans: Wait, look at our old postcard: Save two chairs for the baker and the teacher!
He was the music teacher who played Friday duets with your aunt!
He just asked me who finally finished the second half of her May waltz!
What did he say when he heard my sixteen bars through the window, Ernesto?
He had tears in his eyes: he said it sounded just like her voice!
Did you invite him to our grand opening this Friday at six o'clock sharp?!
He promised to bring his violin and ten more neighbours from our street!
Ten more neighbours?! Rocio is going to need twice as many lemons by Friday!
Until next time!

words.gloss: next (hasta la próxima = until next time)

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.text: Acabo de llegar del mercado.
examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.text: Es una pieza antigua.
examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Used for the formal opening of a shop, café, or exhibition, as well as opening hours (horario de apertura).

examples.text: Este viernes celebramos la gran apertura del café del patio.
examples.trans: This Friday we celebrate the grand opening of the courtyard café.

examples.text: El horario de apertura de la librería está en la puerta.
examples.trans: The bookshop's opening hours are on the door.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.text: El año está aquí.
examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.text: Abro la cafetería cada mañana.
examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.

examples.text: Cada habitación tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.text: Es una pieza caliente.
examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Plural compases drops the written accent.

examples.text: Los cuatro primeros compases suenan muy alegres.
examples.trans: The first four bars sound very cheerful.

examples.text: Lleva el compás despacio con la mano izquierda.
examples.trans: Keep the beat slowly with your left hand.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

conocer.gloss: to know (a person or place); to meet

meanings.en: to know (a person or place); to meet
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg conozco; preterite conocí often means 'met for the first time'.

examples.text: Conozco muy bien este barrio.
examples.trans: I know this neighbourhood very well.

examples.text: Ayer conocimos al nuevo vecino.
examples.trans: Yesterday we met the new neighbour.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Compound numeral (diez + y + seis); carries an acute accent on -éis.

examples.text: Faltan dieciséis compases para cerrar la segunda parte.
examples.trans: Sixteen bars are missing to close the second part.

examples.text: Hemos preparado dieciséis tazas blancas en la bandeja.
examples.trans: We set out sixteen white cups on the tray.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.text: Disculpe, ¿sabe qué hora es?
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: El doble de... means 'double the amount of...'.

examples.text: El doble está aquí.
examples.trans: The double is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dobles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doubles from the door.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Plural los dúos.

examples.text: El dúo está aquí.
examples.trans: The duet is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dúos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the duets from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Third-person feminine singular pronoun.

examples.text: Ella conoce muy bien esta calle.
examples.trans: She knows this street very well.

examples.text: Este regalo es para ella.
examples.trans: This gift is for her.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Por fin = finally.

examples.text: El fin está aquí.
examples.trans: The end is here.

examples.text: Vemos los fines desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ends from the door.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Igual que = just like / the same as.

examples.text: Es una pieza igual.
examples.trans: It is a same piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

invitar.gloss: to invite; to treat (pick up the bill)

meanings.en: to invite; to treat (pick up the bill)
meanings.note: Invita la casa means 'it is on the house'.

examples.text: Hoy invito yo al café de la mañana.
examples.trans: Today morning coffee is my treat.

examples.text: Nos invitaron a cenar el sábado.
examples.trans: They invited us to dinner on Saturday.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: El limón está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Antepenultimate stress (esdrújula); tener lágrimas en los ojos = to have tears in one's eyes.

examples.text: Al oír el viejo vals, el vecino tenía lágrimas de emoción en los ojos.
examples.trans: On hearing the old waltz, the neighbour had tears of emotion in his eyes.

examples.text: Cortar cebolla siempre me saca alguna lágrima.
examples.trans: Chopping onions always brings a tear to my eye.

meanings.note: Months are written with a small letter in Spanish: el diez de mayo.

examples.text: Mi cumpleaños es en mayo.
examples.trans: My birthday is in May.

examples.text: Llegamos el tres de mayo.
examples.trans: We arrive on the third of May.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.text: La mitad está aquí.
examples.trans: The half is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mitades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halves from the door.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco más de té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?

examples.text: Es la habitación más tranquila.
examples.trans: It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Clases de música = music lessons.

examples.text: La música es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The music is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la música.
examples.trans: We talk about the music.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Necesito un bolígrafo para firmar.
examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.

examples.text: ¿Necesitan ustedes alguna toalla más?
examples.trans: Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.text: El número está aquí.
examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.text: El ojo está aquí.
examples.trans: The eye is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ojos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: A woman baker is la panadera; the shop is la panadería.

examples.text: El panadero empieza a trabajar a las cuatro.
examples.trans: The baker starts work at four.

examples.text: La panadera nos guarda dos barras de pan.
examples.trans: The baker keeps two loaves of bread for us.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Short for tarjeta postal.

examples.text: La postal está aquí.
examples.trans: The postcard is here.

examples.text: Vemos las postales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the postcards from the door.

meanings.note: Preguntar asks a question; pedir asks for an item or favour.

examples.text: Pregunto en la farmacia por la calle.
examples.trans: I ask at the pharmacy about the street.

examples.text: Una clienta preguntó por el desayuno.
examples.trans: A guest asked about breakfast.

meanings.note: Feminine form: la profesora; used in Spain for schoolteachers, music teachers, and university professors alike.

examples.text: El antiguo profesor de violín vivía en el número diez de nuestra calle.
examples.trans: The former violin teacher lived at number ten on our street.

examples.text: Nuestra profesora de música nos enseñó a tocar este vals.
examples.trans: Our music teacher taught us how to play this waltz.

meanings.note: Lo prometo = I promise.

examples.text: Te prometo volver antes de las siete.
examples.trans: I promise you I will return before seven.

examples.text: Prometieron visitarnos la semana próxima.
examples.trans: They promised to visit us next week.

meanings.note: El próximo invierno = next winter.

examples.text: Es una pieza próxima.
examples.trans: It is a next piece.

examples.text: ¡Compra las dos! Una válvula de repuesto salva también el próximo invierno.
examples.trans: Buy both! A spare valve saves next winter too.

punto.gloss: dot; point (en punto = on the dot; a punto de = about to)

meanings.en: dot; point (en punto = on the dot; a punto de = about to)
meanings.note: A las nueve en punto = at nine o'clock sharp.

examples.text: El punto está aquí.
examples.trans: The dot is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puntos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the dots from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.text: ¿Quiere usted café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: Lo abrí sin querer.
examples.trans: I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.text: ¿Quién ha dejado este sobre aquí?
examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?

examples.text: ¿De quién es esta maleta azul?
examples.trans: Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.text: Es una pieza segunda.
examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.text: El señor está aquí.
examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Wooden or folding chair.

examples.text: La silla está aquí.
examples.trans: The chair is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the chairs from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.text: La taza está aquí.
examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

terminar.gloss: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)

meanings.en: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Termino mi turno a las tres.
examples.trans: I finish my shift at three.

examples.text: Terminamos de pintar antes de comer.
examples.trans: We finished painting before lunch.

meanings.note: Small local shop.

examples.text: La tienda está aquí.
examples.trans: The shop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tiendas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shops from the door.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.text: ¿Qué quiere tomar para desayunar?
examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?

examples.text: Toma, aquí tienes la linterna.
examples.trans: Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Irregular: traigo, traje; future traeré.

examples.text: Ahora mismo le traigo una cuchara.
examples.trans: I will bring you a spoon right now.

examples.text: Ayer trajo flores del mercado.
examples.trans: Yesterday she brought flowers from the market.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.text: El té está aquí.
examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el tío ('uncle').

examples.text: La tía de Ernesto tocaba el piano todos los viernes.
examples.trans: Ernesto's aunt played the piano every Friday.

examples.text: Mi tía prepara el mejor bizcocho de limón del barrio.
examples.trans: My aunt bakes the best lemon sponge cake in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person plural verbs (pasen ustedes).

examples.text: ¿Tienen ustedes una reserva?
examples.trans: Do you all have a reservation?

examples.text: El patio es para todos ustedes.
examples.trans: The courtyard is for all of you.

meanings.note: Plural los valses.

examples.text: El piano suena precioso con este vals antiguo.
examples.trans: The piano sounds lovely with this old waltz.

examples.text: Un vals tiene siempre tres tiempos por compás.
examples.trans: A waltz always has three beats per bar.

meanings.note: Feminine: la vecina.

examples.text: El vecino está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vecinos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbours from the door.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.text: El viernes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent mark in the plural because -es makes it naturally stressed on -li-: los violines.

examples.text: Nuestro vecino toca el violín desde que tenía ocho años.
examples.trans: Our neighbour has played the violin since he was eight years old.

examples.text: El violín y el piano sonaron juntos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: The violin and the piano sounded together under the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Plural las voces; en voz baja = in a low voice.

examples.text: La voz está aquí.
examples.trans: The voice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las voces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the voices from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Accented él ('he/him') is distinct from unaccented article el ('the').

examples.text: Él trabaja en el ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: He works at City Hall.

examples.text: Sube a hablar con él un minuto.
examples.trans: Go upstairs and talk to him for a minute.
